claims.text: A secondary low-energy laser re-melting pass after each deposited layer will reduce microstructural segregation in L-PBF AlCrFeNiSi.
The secondary re-melting pass will relieve residual thermal stresses in L-PBF AlCrFeNiSi.
The secondary re-melting pass will lower defect formation in L-PBF AlCrFeNiSi.
Conventionally single-scanned L-PBF AlCrFeNiSi tends to develop segregation, residual stresses, and associated mechanical defects.
The secondary pass should be applied immediately after each layer at approximately 20% lower laser energy than the primary pass.
Optimizing laser power, scan speed, and scan strategy permits control of energy input during L-PBF.
The proposed re-melting treatment can homogenize the melt pool and partially re-dissolve early dendritic structures.
Excessive laser energy can cause keyholing, so the secondary-pass energy must remain below the keyholing regime.
The selected secondary-pass energy can avoid undesirable grain coarsening.
The secondary pass enhances melt-pool homogenization and dissolves early-solidified dendrite boundaries.
Reheating a freshly solidified layer promotes additional mixing of the alloy components.
Additional mixing reduces chemical inhomogeneity and inter-dendritic segregation.
The secondary pass reduces residual thermal gradients and thereby mitigates internal stress.
Reduced segregation and internal stress produce a more uniform microstructure with fewer segregated boundaries.
Reduced segregation, residual stress, and defects lead to improved mechanical integrity.
Relative to single-scan L-PBF, re-melted AlCrFeNiSi will have a more uniform microstructure, less inter-dendritic segregation, lower residual stress, and better mechanical performance.
Insufficient energy may produce lack-of-fusion or balling, while excessive energy may produce keyhole porosity.
The magnitude of improvement may depend on machine-specific factors and powder characteristics.
